title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Sport Science (2016)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Sport Science (2016). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: Athletes training at high altitudes might require special attention due to:
questions.explanation: Decreased air pressure at high altitudes can affect oxygen availability.

questions.questionText: Which exercise primarily targets cardiovascular endurance?
questions.explanation: Running is a primary exercise for improving cardiovascular endurance.

questions.questionText: Which function involves ensuring that performance does not deviate from standards?
questions.explanation: Controlling involves monitoring performance to ensure standards are met.

questions.questionText: What does the Inverted-U Hypothesis suggest about the relationship between arousal and performance?
options: Performance improves with increased arousal up to a certain point.
There's no relationship between arousal and performance.
questions.explanation: The Inverted-U Hypothesis indicates that performance improves with arousal to an optimal point.

questions.questionText: Which of the following best defines 'measurement'?
options: Judging the quality of student's performance.
questions.explanation: Measurement involves quantifying specific attributes or characteristics.

questions.questionText: What is the primary concern when managing a sports facility?
questions.explanation: Safety and functionality are critical in managing sports facilities.

questions.questionText: What is the primary goal when designing an exercise program for individuals with mobility impairments?
questions.explanation: The main goal is to improve mobility and independence for individuals with mobility impairments.

questions.questionText: Which sport was originally developed as a training exercise for businessmen?
questions.explanation: Volleyball was created by William G. Morgan in 1895 as a less strenuous alternative to basketball for businessmen at the YMCA.

questions.questionText: Who is known as the 'Father of the Modern Olympics'?
questions.explanation: Pierre de Coubertin is recognized as the founder of the modern Olympic Games.

questions.questionText: What is the primary characteristic of intellectual disabilities?
questions.explanation: Intellectual disabilities are characterized by below-average intellectual functioning.

questions.questionText: How often should an average adult perform moderate aerobic activity?
questions.explanation: Adults should engage in moderate aerobic activity 3 to 5 times a week, totaling at least 150 minutes per week according to most health guidelines.

questions.questionText: What is the primary purpose of sport coaching?
questions.explanation: The main purpose of sport coaching is to develop athletes' skills.

questions.questionText: What is a key coaching skill related to effective communication?
questions.explanation: Active listening is crucial for effective communication in coaching.

questions.questionText: What does the shuttle run test measure?
questions.explanation: The shuttle run test is designed to measure agility.

questions.questionText: During prolonged aerobic exercise, what is the primary source of energy?
questions.explanation: Fatty acids are the primary energy source during prolonged aerobic exercise, especially after glycogen stores begin to deplete (typically after 20-30 minutes of sustained activity).

questions.questionText: Which coaching plan typically covers a single day's training activities?
questions.explanation: A daily plan outlines training activities for a single day.

questions.questionText: Who is credited with inventing basketball?
questions.explanation: Dr. James Naismith invented basketball in 1891 while working as a physical education instructor at the International YMCA Training School (now Springfield College) in Massachusetts.

questions.questionText: What is the name of the line that divides the volleyball court into two equal halves?
questions.explanation: The centerline divides the volleyball court into two equal halves.

questions.questionText: Which of these is NOT one of the five components of physical fitness?
questions.explanation: The five components of physical fitness are cardiovascular endurance, muscular strength, muscular endurance, flexibility, and body composition. Bone density, while important for health, is not one of these five primary components.

questions.questionText: Which term describes a state of mental or emotional strain?
questions.explanation: Stress refers to a state of mental or emotional strain.

questions.questionText: In sports management, which function is concerned with budget allocation and revenue generation?
questions.explanation: Financial planning involves budget allocation and revenue generation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is essential for the smooth execution of a sports tournament?
questions.explanation: Effective coordination and communication are crucial for executing a sports tournament.

questions.questionText: How many touches are a team allowed before the ball must cross the net in volleyball?
questions.explanation: A volleyball team is allowed a maximum of 3 touches (contacts) before the ball must cross over the net to the opponent's side.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a trait of Type A personality?
questions.explanation: Patience is not typically associated with Type A personality traits.

questions.questionText: Evaluation in physical education mainly focuses on:
options: Making decisions based on collected data.
questions.explanation: Evaluation involves making decisions based on collected data.

questions.questionText: Which coaching philosophy prioritizes the development of an athlete's character and values?
questions.explanation: Athlete-centered coaching focuses on developing character and values.

questions.questionText: Which process occurs in the mitochondria and requires oxygen?
questions.explanation: The Krebs Cycle (or citric acid cycle) occurs in the mitochondria and requires oxygen. It is part of aerobic cellular respiration, converting acetyl-CoA into carbon dioxide while generating high-energy electron carriers.

questions.questionText: Which of the following populations may require specialized consideration in sports medicine due to decreased bone density?
questions.explanation: Postmenopausal women often experience decreased bone density.

questions.questionText: Dr. James Naismith is credited with inventing which sport in 1891?
questions.explanation: Dr. James Naismith invented basketball in 1891 at the International YMCA Training School in Springfield, Massachusetts. He created it as an indoor game that could be played during winter months.

questions.questionText: Which piece of apparatus was traditionally used by men only in gymnastics?
questions.explanation: Rings were traditionally used by men in gymnastics.

questions.questionText: In volleyball, how many players are typically on each side of the court during a game?
questions.explanation: A standard volleyball game has 6 players on each side.

questions.questionText: The gymnasion in ancient Greece served as a training facility for what?
questions.explanation: The gymnasion was primarily for training in athletic events.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of cerebral palsy?
questions.explanation: Cerebral palsy typically does not include above-average intellectual functioning.

questions.questionText: In pole vault, what do athletes use to propel themselves over a bar?
questions.explanation: Athletes use a pole to propel themselves in pole vaulting.

questions.questionText: Which of the following ancient civilizations had a strong emphasis on physical education?
questions.explanation: All listed civilizations emphasized physical education.

questions.questionText: Who is known as the 'Father of the Modern Olympics'?
questions.explanation: Baron Pierre de Coubertin, a French educator and historian, is recognized as the father of the modern Olympic Games. He founded the International Olympic Committee (IOC) in 1894 and organized the first modern Olympics in Athens in 1896.

questions.questionText: Which move in basketball involves a player rotating the ball around the back?
questions.explanation: The behind-the-back dribble involves rotating the ball around the back.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a primary concern when returning an athlete to play post-injury?
options: Making sure they have new equipment
Ensuring they are pain-free and at minimal risk of re-injury
Ensuring they have a new coach
questions.explanation: The primary concern is ensuring the athlete is pain-free and at minimal risk of re-injury.

questions.questionText: Measurement in physical education primarily deals with:
options: Collecting data about a specific attribute.
questions.explanation: Measurement focuses on collecting data about specific attributes.

questions.questionText: How many points is a free throw worth in basketball?
questions.explanation: A free throw is worth 1 point in basketball. It is awarded after certain fouls and is shot from the free throw line without any defensive pressure.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a part of a coach's role in preparing athletes for competitions?
questions.explanation: Providing medical care is typically not a coach's role but rather the responsibility of medical professionals such as team physicians, athletic trainers, or physiotherapists. Coaches focus on training, tactics, and performance enhancement.

questions.questionText: In adapted physical education, what does the term 'inclusion' refer to?
options: Excluding students with disabilities from physical activities
Adapting activities to meet individual needs
Integrating students with disabilities into regular physical education classes
questions.explanation: Inclusion refers to integrating students with disabilities into regular classes.

questions.questionText: Which diagnostic tool is most commonly used to view soft tissue injuries in sports medicine?
questions.explanation: MRI is commonly used to view soft tissue injuries.

questions.questionText: Which of the following results in an indirect free-kick in football?
questions.explanation: Dangerous play results in an indirect free-kick.

questions.questionText: Which of the following team sports originated in England during the 19th century?
questions.explanation: Football originated in England during the 19th century.

questions.questionText: Which technique involves a rapid hand movement on the parallel bars or the uneven bars?
questions.explanation: The kip is a technique involving rapid hand movement on the bars.

questions.questionText: Which type of anxiety is temporary and specific to a particular situation?
questions.explanation: State anxiety is temporary and situation-specific.

questions.questionText: The modern Olympic Games were first held in which year?
questions.explanation: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece in 1896, organized by the International Olympic Committee under the leadership of Baron Pierre de Coubertin.

questions.questionText: Which civilization emphasized physical training mainly for military purposes?
questions.explanation: The Romans emphasized physical training for military purposes.

questions.questionText: Which of the following best defines fitness?
questions.explanation: Fitness is defined as the ability to perform daily tasks.

questions.questionText: EPOC stands for?
questions.explanation: EPOC stands for Excess Post-exercise Oxygen Consumption, which refers to the increased oxygen intake that occurs during the recovery period after strenuous exercise to restore the body to its pre-exercise state.

questions.questionText: In volleyball, what is it called when a player hits the ball over the net with great force and speed?
questions.explanation: A spike, also known as an attack or hit, is when a player forcefully hits the ball over the net aiming for the opponent's court, typically after a set from a teammate.

questions.questionText: What is the term for the process of modifying physical activities to meet the individual needs of students with disabilities?
questions.explanation: Adaptation refers to modifying activities for individual needs.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT considered a common category of disability in adapted physical education?
questions.explanation: Cultural differences are not a common category of disability.

questions.questionText: Who is primarily responsible for ensuring all logistics are in place during a sports event?
questions.explanation: The event coordinator is responsible for logistics during a sports event.

questions.questionText: What is the main objective of volleyball?
options: Score points by hitting the ball over the net
questions.explanation: The objective of volleyball is to score points by hitting the ball over the net.

questions.questionText: What is the historical origin of volleyball?
questions.explanation: Volleyball originated in the United States.

questions.questionText: Which of the following conditions often requires adaptations in aquatic activities due to a risk of overheating?
questions.explanation: Down syndrome may require adaptations in aquatic activities due to overheating risks.

questions.questionText: Chronic, or ongoing, anxiety is also known as:
questions.explanation: Trait anxiety refers to chronic or ongoing anxiety.

questions.questionText: The immediate source of energy for muscle contraction is?
questions.explanation: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) is the immediate source of energy for muscle contraction. The breakdown of ATP to ADP (adenosine diphosphate) releases energy that powers muscle fiber contraction.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a violation in basketball?
questions.explanation: Traveling is a violation in basketball.

questions.questionText: How does high motivation generally affect an athlete's performance?
questions.explanation: High motivation generally increases an athlete's performance.

questions.questionText: Which event does not involve jumping?
questions.explanation: Shot put does not involve jumping.

questions.questionText: Handball has its origins in which region?
questions.explanation: Handball originated in Europe.

questions.questionText: In handball, how many steps can a player take without dribbling the ball?
options: Unlimited as long as they bounce the ball
questions.explanation: A player can take three steps without dribbling the ball in handball.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a primary management function?
questions.explanation: Promoting is not considered a primary management function.

questions.questionText: How many fouls does a player have to commit to be fouled out in an NBA game?
questions.explanation: In the NBA (National Basketball Association), a player is fouled out after committing 6 personal fouls during a game.

questions.questionText: Which part of the hand should be used for a proper volleyball serve?
questions.explanation: For a standard underhand serve, the palm or heel of the hand is typically used. For overhand serves, players may use the heel of the hand or a closed fist, depending on the serving technique.

questions.questionText: In sports management, what function involves setting goals and determining how to achieve them?
questions.explanation: Planning involves setting goals and determining how to achieve them.

questions.questionText: What is the FIRST step in organizing a sports event?
questions.explanation: The first step in organizing a sports event is planning.

questions.questionText: The ancient Olympic Games were held in which country?
questions.explanation: The ancient Olympic Games were held in Olympia, Greece, from approximately 776 BCE to 393 CE. They were held every four years in honor of Zeus.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a primary responsibility of a coach when conducting fitness tests?
questions.explanation: Documenting athlete performance is a primary responsibility of a coach.

questions.questionText: What should be the primary focus before starting any exercise regimen?
questions.explanation: Safety should be the primary focus before starting any exercise regimen.

questions.questionText: How many original rules were there in basketball?
questions.explanation: There were originally 13 rules in basketball.

questions.questionText: Which system provides oxygen and nutrients to the body during exercise?
questions.explanation: The cardiovascular system (heart, blood vessels, and blood) transports oxygen and nutrients to working muscles during exercise, while removing waste products like carbon dioxide and lactic acid.

questions.questionText: Which of these is NOT a basic body position in gymnastics?
questions.explanation: Dive is not considered a basic body position in gymnastics.

questions.questionText: In which year were the first modern Olympic Games held?
questions.explanation: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece in 1896, reviving the ancient tradition after an initiative by Baron Pierre de Coubertin.

questions.questionText: Cardiac output is the product of what two variables?
questions.explanation: Cardiac output is calculated as stroke volume (amount of blood pumped per beat) multiplied by heart rate (beats per minute), measured in liters per minute.

questions.questionText: Which professional typically provides immediate care to an injured athlete?
questions.explanation: An athletic trainer typically provides immediate care to injured athletes.

questions.questionText: Which type of disability is characterized by difficulties in social interaction and communication, as well as repetitive behaviors?
questions.explanation: Autism spectrum disorder is characterized by social interaction difficulties and repetitive behaviors.

questions.questionText: The World Health Organization defines health as:
options: state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being
questions.explanation: The WHO defines health as a state of complete well-being.

questions.questionText: Which test measures muscular strength of the upper body?
questions.explanation: Push-ups measure upper body muscular strength.

questions.questionText: Which organ is primarily responsible for delivering oxygen to the muscles during exercise?
questions.explanation: The heart is primarily responsible for pumping oxygenated blood to deliver oxygen to the muscles during exercise. The lungs oxygenate the blood, but it's the heart that delivers it to the working muscles.

questions.questionText: What is the first position a beginner gymnast learns on the balance beam?
questions.explanation: The mount is typically the first position learned on the balance beam.

questions.questionText: Which country is considered the birthplace of gymnastics?
questions.explanation: Greece is considered the birthplace of gymnastics.

questions.questionText: What is the standard time for a quarter in an NBA game?
questions.explanation: Each quarter in an NBA game is 12 minutes long, making a full game 48 minutes of playing time (excluding timeouts, halftime, and other stoppages).

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of an annual coaching plan?
questions.explanation: An annual coaching plan is used to set long-term objectives.

questions.questionText: Which coaching philosophy emphasizes winning at all costs?
questions.explanation: Outcome-oriented coaching prioritizes winning above all else.

questions.questionText: In which country was basketball invented?
questions.explanation: Basketball was invented in the USA.

questions.questionText: Which theory suggests that people are motivated to perform to receive an external reward?
questions.explanation: Extrinsic motivation refers to performing for external rewards.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of a sensory impairment?
questions.explanation: Visual impairment is a type of sensory impairment.

questions.questionText: In volleyball, which player wears a different colored jersey?
questions.explanation: The libero wears a different colored jersey in volleyball.

questions.questionText: How many players start on the field for each team in Handball?
questions.explanation: Each team in handball starts with 7 players on the field.

questions.questionText: In which position are the gymnast's legs straight and together, and the body bent at the hips?
questions.explanation: In the pike position, the legs are straight and together with the body bent at the hips.

questions.questionText: What is the maximum number of hits a team is allowed to make before sending the ball over the net in volleyball?
questions.explanation: According to volleyball rules, a team is allowed a maximum of 3 hits (contacts) before the ball must cross over to the opponent's side. These typically include a pass/dig, a set, and an attack.

questions.questionText: A lateral ankle sprain typically affects which ligament?
questions.explanation: The anterior talofibular ligament is commonly affected in lateral ankle sprains.

questions.questionText: Where were the ancient Olympic Games originally held?
questions.explanation: The ancient Olympic Games were held in the sanctuary of Olympia in the northwestern Peloponnese region of Greece, near the city of Elis.

questions.questionText: When did gymnastics first debut in the modern Olympic Games?
questions.explanation: Gymnastics was part of the program at the first modern Olympic Games held in Athens in 1896. Men's artistic gymnastics has been included in every Olympics since then, while women's gymnastics was first included in 1928.

questions.questionText: In the sit and reach test, what is primarily being measured?
questions.explanation: The sit and reach test primarily measures flexibility.

questions.questionText: What is a 'dig' in volleyball?
options: quick set to the middle hitter
defensive technique to pass a spiked ball
questions.explanation: A dig is a defensive technique used to pass a spiked ball.
